market_context: United States; general household dishwasher maintenance with model-specific manufacturer guidance.
title: How to Clean a Dishwasher

seo.title: How to Clean a Dishwasher: Filter, Spray Arms and Seals
seo.meta_description: Effective dishwasher cleaning starts with the filter and spray arms. Learn what to remove, what to wipe, and when odor or standing water points to another problem.
seo.search_intent: Clean a dishwasher to restore wash performance and prevent odors, residue and clogs without inappropriate products.

excerpt: Empty the dishwasher, clean the filter and spray arms first, and wipe the gasket and door edges. Then run a maintenance cycle only if the manufacturer recommends it. Do not use hand dish soap or mix cleaners.
content_html:
When a dishwasher starts smelling odd or leaving grit on dishes that used to come out clean, it is easy to assume the machine has simply stopped washing well. Often the explanation is more physical: water is being circulated past a loaded filter, partially blocked spray arms or door edges that never receive a direct wash.

A useful cleaning session starts with those parts, not with pouring in something fragrant and hoping for a reset. Remove physical debris first; then use a maintenance cycle or dishwasher cleaner only if the manufacturer calls for it.

Empty the machine and inspect the bottom

Pull out the racks and look around the filter and sump area. An olive pit, label, shard of glass or larger food fragment can interfere with drainage or water circulation. If you suspect broken glass, use cut-resistant gloves and do not reach blindly into the sump.

Check the owner's manual before removing the filter or spray arms. Most modern dishwashers have serviceable filters, but the locking mechanism differs by model.

The filter is the place to start

The filter protects the pump from larger debris and helps keep food particles from redepositing on dishes. That also means it is designed to collect soil.

Remove it according to the manual. Many designs twist and lift out from the floor of the tub. Rinse under warm running water and use mild dish soap and a soft brush for stuck-on debris. Avoid wire brushes or abrasive pads that can damage the mesh.

Before reinstalling it, wipe visible debris from the filter well. Lock the filter back into place. A loose filter can allow particles into the pump or back into the wash water.

Spray-arm holes need to stay open

If the filter is reasonably clean but dishes are still coming out with dried soil, inspect the rotating spray arms. Food particles and mineral deposits can block individual jets and change how water reaches the load.

When your model allows the arms to be removed, rinse them with warm water. Bosch recommends clearing blocked holes with a toothpick. Do not enlarge the openings with drill bits or thick metal tools; the jets are sized and angled for a reason.

Also spin the arms by hand after loading. Tall plates, pan handles and utensils can stop an arm from turning, creating a washing problem that looks like a dirty machine.

The door gasket and edges do not wash themselves

The center of the tub is sprayed on every cycle, but the rubber seal, hinges and portions of the door sit outside that direct spray. Wipe them with a damp cloth and a little mild soap if needed.

Pay attention to the lower door edge, where grease and debris can collect out of sight when the machine is closed. Wipe the gasket dry afterward so you do not leave a sticky film.

Hard-water scale is a different problem from grease

A chalky film, cloudy glassware or hard deposits around spray holes point toward minerals. Brownish grease and odor suggest food soil and detergent residue.

Do not treat both problems by mixing household chemicals. Manufacturers sell or recommend specific machine cleaners and descalers. Follow those directions and never combine different products inside the dishwasher. In particular, do not mix chlorine-containing products with acids or vinegar.

Hand dishwashing liquid does not belong in the machine

It is tempting when the dishwasher tablet box is empty: “just a small squirt” of sink soap. Hand dish detergent is designed to foam. Automatic dishwasher detergent is deliberately low-sudsing. Even a modest amount of hand soap can fill the tub with foam and lead to leaks or a very messy cycle.

If you are out of automatic dishwasher detergent, waiting is safer than substituting sink soap.

Use a maintenance cycle after the parts are clean

Once the filter and arms are correctly reinstalled, run an empty cleaning cycle if your model provides one. Use only the program and cleaning product recommended for the appliance. Instructions vary with brand, machine design and water hardness.

When the cycle is finished, let the interior vent and make sure no cleaner residue remains.

How often should you clean a dishwasher?

There is no single interval that fits every household. A filter receiving dishes with lots of solid food debris needs more frequent cleaning than one in a home where large scraps are removed before loading.

You do not need to rinse every plate spotless before loading, but bones, seeds, labels and chunks that cannot dissolve should be scraped into the trash or compost first.

Let the filter itself guide you. If it is coated in debris or starting to smell, you are waiting too long between cleanings.

When cleaning is not the fix

If water still stands in the bottom after the filter and sump are cleaned, the pump makes unusual noises, an error code appears, or the dishwasher has stopped heating or drying, you may be dealing with a mechanical problem rather than routine maintenance.

Leaks, electrical odors and breakers that trip also call for service rather than more cleaning products.

The maintenance principle is simple: a dishwasher cleans well when water can move freely. Keep the filter clear, let the spray arms rotate, open their jets, wipe the areas the spray cannot reach, and treat machine cleaner as the finishing step rather than a substitute for physical cleaning.

faq.question: Why does my dishwasher smell bad?
faq.answer: Odor often comes from debris trapped in the filter, sump area, gasket or lower door edge. Clean those physical areas before relying on a machine cleaner.

faq.question: Can I use regular hand dish soap in a dishwasher?
faq.answer: No. Hand dishwashing liquid creates too much foam and can cause leaks or overflow.

faq.question: How do I clean dishwasher spray arms?
faq.answer: If your model allows removal, rinse the arms with warm water and clear blocked jets with a toothpick or other gentle tool that will not enlarge the holes.

faq.question: What if there is still water in the bottom after cleaning?
faq.answer: Check the filter and owner's manual first. Persistent standing water can indicate a drainage or pump problem that needs diagnosis.
